# Generation-first file integrations

## Generated and handwritten ownership

Keep the file contract in the CodeGen console's checked-in `*-file.yaml`. File CodeGen generates the nullable wire model, mapping, validator, context, processor, and create-only handler; handwritten code should add application behavior and host adapters, not duplicate generated types.

The framework's [InventoryImports example](https://github.com/Avanade/CoreEx/tree/main/tests/CoreEx.Azure.Functions.TestApp/InventoryImports) uses `tests/CoreEx.Azure.Functions.TestApp.CodeGen/inventory-file.yaml` (`name: Inventory`, record `Adjustment`) to generate `InventoryAdjustment`, `InventoryAdjustmentMapping`, `InventoryAdjustmentValidator`, `InventoryContext`, `InventoryProcessor`, and `InventoryHandler` under `InventoryImports/Files`. Its handwritten processor partial uses inherited protected `Services` for coordinator options/reporting, not as the fresh unit provider. Keep per-unit business dependencies in the generated handler's fresh child scope.

The external [JSONL definition example](https://github.com/Avanade/CoreEx/blob/main/tests/CoreEx.CodeGen.Test.Unit/orders-jsonl-file.yaml) generates reusable Address occurrences, order-line/scalar collections, DateTimeOffset conversion, and the same scoped application boundary. Its [integration test](https://github.com/Avanade/CoreEx/blob/main/tests/CoreEx.IO.Test.Unit/GeneratedJsonLinesIntegrationTests.cs) pins replay to immutable bytes and uses an in-memory receipt double to illustrate retry ownership; it does not prove durable deduplication. [Routed JSONL](https://github.com/Avanade/CoreEx/blob/main/tests/CoreEx.CodeGen.Test.Unit/routed-jsonl-file.yaml) adds explicit metadata matches and First/Last checks without making metadata executable. These framework examples are illustrative, not files assumed to exist in a consumer project.

## Blob revisions, reports, and transactions

Keep the native Functions Blob trigger thin and reference `CoreEx.Azure.Storage.Blobs` in the host/storage adapter. Select once with `BlobReadSource.CreateAsync(blob, cancellationToken)`, construct the caller-owned identity from `source.SourceUri.AbsoluteUri` and `source.ETag.ToString()`, and pass `source.OpenReadAsync` as the processor's fresh-stream factory. Both passes carry IfMatch and fail on replacement rather than silently reading new bytes. Use a version/snapshot-specific BlobClient when historical event revisions must be processed; pinning does not retain historical bytes. CoreEx.IO stays Azure-independent.

For standard streamed attempt reporting, use `FileProcessingReporter.RunAsync` with the `CoreEx.Azure.Storage.Blobs` JSONL or CSV adapter, or a composite of both; customize projections as needed and avoid writing the same report again in processor hooks. Composite writes are sequential, not atomic. Alternatively use `BlobJsonlReport` directly for custom lifecycle handling. `CreateName` hashes framed definition/source/revision/attempt components; StartAsync creates without overwrite, WriteAsync appends compact JSONL, and CompleteAsync writes a summary before terminal outcome metadata. Provision containers separately and propagate report failures; the report instance faults after ambiguous writes rather than blindly retrying. The application uses `SqlServerUnitOfWork` and `SqlServerOutboxPublisher` to commit `Items`, `Receipts`, and the outbox write in one SQL Server transaction. Receipt identity excludes the delivery attempt so retries of the same source revision do not repeat already-committed units. This is not a whole-file transaction or an exactly-once trigger/relay guarantee.

For a flat supplier-facing rejection/reconciliation export, use `BlobCsvReport` with explicit columns and required `CsvFormulaHandling`. StartAsync writes one header, WriteAsync accepts ordered invariantly formatted scalar cells with matching width, and CompleteAsync(outcome) updates metadata without a summary row. Standard CSV quoting is not spreadsheet formula protection: choose Reject, PrefixApostrophe or Preserve explicitly, including the treatment of negative numbers. Keep JSONL for heterogeneous operational records; CSV input does not require CSV reporting.

## Publishing accepted units

For file-to-Service-Bus output without a database/outbox, use the configured `IEventPublisher` backed by `ServiceBusPublisher` or a custom registered implementation in each fresh unit-handler scope, add that unit's command and await `PublishAsync(cancellationToken)`. Do not retain an invocation-wide row queue or format/send through a raw `ServiceBusSender`. Direct means bypassing the outbox, not CoreEx; stable command identity and duplicate-tolerant consumers are still required. Preserve configured publisher/subscriber overrides and use the [Functions publishing pattern](../../coreex-functions/references/patterns.md#direct-service-bus-publishing-no-outbox). A raw SDK exception needs a concrete documented requirement.

## Aspire verification boundary

The existing Functions Aspire AppHost orchestrates Azurite, SQL Server, and Functions Core Tools. Its CSV scenario uploads the real input to Azurite, creates an Event Grid-shaped notification with `EventGridExtensionMethods.CreateBlobCreatedEvent`, and posts it through `Test.FunctionsWebhook(...).PostBlobCreatedAsync(...)`. That call simulates notification delivery only because Azurite does not emit Event Grid events; the Functions binding, Blob SDK operations, SQL Server transaction, and Blob report writes are real in the harness.

Do not treat this local runtime test as proof of Azure Event Grid provisioning, authentication, or delivery, and do not claim a new test passed until it has actually run. Local immutable snapshot helpers may support stream-factory tests, but they do not justify a SQLite/database or filesystem-report CLI.
